g.title: recovery
g.text: a failure pauses the print; RESUME diagnoses, continues where it stopped, and pauses again if it fails

g.title: t_n
g.text: or the panel's Load / Unload (no print)

g.title: catch
g.text: one Python command runs the whole macro chain (_TX …)
and catches every error inside it (under gco-routines,
inside its handled region, so the print's run is not faulted)

g.title: chain
g.text: home, heat, cut, retract, rewind, feed,
inlet check, reload, outlet check, CLEAN_NOZZLE, hooks

g.title: fault
g.text: any error: a failed check, the AMS refusing, a hook or CLEAN_NOZZLE
error, homing, a cold extrude, the Stop button.
Records the step, the reason and the target group, puts the toolhead
back where the toolchange started (in a print, unless it had to home
first), and stops the follower once the print is no longer printing

g.title: paused
g.text: PAUSE, the reason in the console;
the file stays open after the T<n> line

g.title: resume
g.text: Mainsail, Fluidd, KlipperScreen or the panel:

g.title: reset
g.text: clears latched unit faults, waits out the unit's 15 s recovery,
clears host errors, re-reads the lanes (operation numbers keep
counting, so the next load's arrival is confirmed)

g.title: diag
g.text: what do the hub (and toolhead) sensors show?

g.title: c_tool
g.text: heat, follower, inlet check, reload, outlet check, CLEAN_NOZZLE

g.title: c_rew
g.text: then the feed and the toolhead part

g.title: c_feed
g.text: the feed, then the toolhead part

g.title: note
g.text: OpenAMS never retries on its own:
the AMS retries before it reports a failure.
Reset alone moves nothing and resumes nothing,
and keeps an unfinished toolchange for RESUME.
A print's fault is dropped when the print ends.
With gco-routines the retry inside RESUME runs
